blocks.name: immediate_generator
blocks.responsibility: Generate I-, S-, B-, U-, and J-type immediates combinationally.
blocks.design_rationale: The formulas remain correct; this block needs no M-specific hardware.

blocks.name: register_file
blocks.responsibility: Provide 32 32-bit integer registers with two asynchronous read ports, one rising-edge write port, asynchronous active-high reset, and hardwired-zero x0.
blocks.design_rationale: Isolates architectural state and asynchronous operand reads, keeping the single-cycle datapath simple and register behavior easy to test.

blocks.name: alu
blocks.responsibility: Perform RV32I arithmetic, logic, shifts, and signed and unsigned comparisons selected by an operation control input.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeps datapath operations and comparison semantics in one combinational block, supporting focused verification and avoiding unnecessary pipeline state.

blocks.name: m_unit
blocks.responsibility: Produce the selected 32-bit M result from two register operands and funct3, including defined division-by-zero and signed-overflow results.
blocks.design_rationale: A separately testable combinational unit supplies the result within the existing single cycle. MULHSU extends its signed and unsigned operands appropriately; division and remainder guard special cases before using numeric_std operators.

blocks.name: decoder
blocks.responsibility: Decode instruction controls and identify M instructions for M-result writeback.
blocks.design_rationale: An explicit M selector avoids redefining the approved ALU control encodings. M instructions assert register write but no memory or control-flow side effects.

blocks.name: cpu
blocks.responsibility: Execute RV32IM instructions in one cycle through the specified external interface.
blocks.design_rationale: Only register writeback gains a new result source. M instructions still advance PC by four and never assert data_write.

notes: Use only ieee.std_logic_1164 and ieee.numeric_std. The decoder's wb_select encodings should distinguish ALU result, load data, PC+4, and U-immediate; AUIPC uses PC as the ALU first operand. Branch conditions use funct3 together with the ALU comparison outputs. Stores drive the unshifted rs2 value and select byte, halfword, or word width; loads select and extend the addressed subword from the asynchronously supplied aligned word.
